name: Establishing Therapeutic Alliance and Psychoeducation
description: The therapist initiates treatment by building rapport, establishing collaborative goals, and educating the patient about the CBT model, including the connection between thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and physical sensations.

goal.objective: Build trust and understanding, foster engagement, and orient the patient to CBT principles.

success_levels.ideal: Patient expresses trust, feels understood, grasps CBT concepts, and is motivated to engage.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient demonstrates basic understanding and willingness to try CBT techniques.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains skeptical, disengaged, or confused about CBT.

goal.reward_hint: Verbalized understanding, commitment to try, patient asking questions about CBT.

states: Patient is unfamiliar or unsure about CBT.
Patient expresses skepticism, reluctance, or questions about the therapy process.

micro_actions.name: Initiate rapport-building
micro_actions.description: Greet the patient warmly, express interest in their experiences, and acknowledge any initial concerns or nervousness to foster trust.
states: Patient is anxious or expresses skepticism.

micro_actions.name: Provide psychoeducation about CBT
micro_actions.description: Explain the CBT model in simple terms, including the link between thoughts, feelings, behaviors, and physical sensations.
states: Patient does not understand or is new to CBT.
Initial session or when patient asks about therapy.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively set expectations and goals
micro_actions.description: Ask what the patient hopes to gain from therapy and clarify expectations for sessions; align treatment focus to their needs.
states: Patient unsure about objectives of therapy.

micro_actions.name: Address doubts and provide validation
micro_actions.description: Acknowledge any skepticism or reluctance, validate the patient's feelings, and clarify misconceptions about CBT.

micro_actions.name: Encourage questions and feedback
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to ask questions about CBT, treatment process, or procedures, and openly address their queries.
states: Any point where patient seems uncertain.

name: Mood and Thought Identification
description: The therapist guides the patient in identifying, labeling, and tracking moods and automatic thoughts using structured tools such as worksheets and thought records.

goal.objective: Increase patient awareness and articulation of thoughts and emotional states as foundational CBT skills.

success_levels.ideal: Patient can accurately distinguish and record moods and thoughts in diverse situations.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient can identify and label moods and thoughts with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unable or unwilling to differentiate or report moods/thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes worksheets, speaks in terms of identified thoughts and moods.

states: Early treatment when the patient struggles to specify or express emotions/thoughts.
Patient reports mixed or unclear emotional experiences.

micro_actions.name: Prompt mood identification
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to describe recent situations and to label the mood they felt in one word (e.g., 'sad', 'anxious').
states: Patient appears upset but cannot specify emotion.
Early or ongoing sessions focusing on mood awareness.

micro_actions.name: Guide mood intensity rating
micro_actions.description: Request that the patient rate mood intensity on a 0-100 scale or similar tool and facilitate use of worksheets for tracking.
states: When identifying mood is insufficient for understanding severity.

micro_actions.name: Prompt automatic thought identification
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient what went through their mind during a specific mood episode and encourage articulation of words, images, or memories.
states: Patient describes a strong emotion without connecting it to thoughts.

micro_actions.name: Clarify differences between moods, thoughts, and behaviors
micro_actions.description: Help the patient distinguish moods from thoughts and behaviors through specific questions (e.g., 'Is this what you felt, thought, or did?').

micro_actions.name: Guide completion of mood/thought worksheets
micro_actions.description: Provide and walk through structured worksheets, helping the patient fill out mood ratings, situation descriptions, and automatic thoughts.
states: Patient is ready to record and track data.

micro_actions.name: Review and reinforce tracking skills
micro_actions.description: Periodically review completed records, give feedback, and encourage consistent tracking of moods and thoughts.
states: Patient has started or completed entries.

name: Case Conceptualization and Collaborative Formulation
description: Therapist and patient work together to understand how specific life events, thoughts, moods, behaviors, and physical reactions contribute to the presenting concerns via CBT models.

goal.objective: Develop shared understanding of patient’s problems and formulation of CBT targets.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient co-create a clear, personalized CBT case formulation.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient understands how events connect to thoughts/moods with therapist direction.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Formulation remains unclear or patient is unable to relate to the conceptual model.

goal.reward_hint: Patient restates the formulation in own words, agrees with the targets.

states: Once presenting problems and basic psychoeducation are complete.
Patient is open to understanding triggers and maintaining factors.

micro_actions.name: Elicit recent life events and narratives
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to share details of recent situations and experiences related to presenting problems for context.

micro_actions.name: Guide completion of conceptual model worksheets
micro_actions.description: Introduce and collaboratively fill out models (e.g., five-part CBT model) mapping situations, moods, thoughts, behaviors, and physical reactions.
states: Patient needs visual or structured support.

micro_actions.name: Draw real-time connections between domains
micro_actions.description: Point out patterns linking thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and reinforce awareness of cyclic effects (e.g., how thoughts drive mood).
states: Worksheet or open dialogue on triggers and symptoms.

micro_actions.name: Encourage patient articulation and reflection
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to describe, restate, or reflect upon their understanding of the case formulation, reinforcing shared understanding.

micro_actions.name: Provide targeted psychoeducation when needed
micro_actions.description: Clarify the differences between related conditions (e.g., depression and anxiety) and explain how symptoms fit into the formulation.

name: Goal Setting and Action Planning
description: The therapist guides the patient to set specific, measurable goals and develop actionable plans to address identified problems.

goal.objective: Establish clear behavioral and emotional change targets, enhance motivation.

success_levels.ideal: Patient articulates meaningful, measurable goals and participates in designing action plans.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient sets basic goals and agrees to try therapist-proposed plans.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unable to set goals or rejects planning process.

goal.reward_hint: Patient selects goals and contributes suggestions for action steps.

states: After problem identification and some skill acquisition.
Patient expresses desire for change or improvement.
Patient is ready for next steps beyond insight.

micro_actions.name: Elicit patient goals
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to state or write down two or more personal, observable, and measurable goals for therapy.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate goal prioritization and discussion
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each goal, and collaboratively select focus areas.

micro_actions.name: Assist in action step design
micro_actions.description: Support the patient in detailing concrete, stepwise actions toward each goal, including timing and measurable outcomes.
states: Patient is ready to move from goals to actions.

micro_actions.name: Explore potential barriers and coping strategies
micro_actions.description: Ask about anticipated obstacles and brainstorm strategies to address them collaboratively.

micro_actions.name: Encourage documentation and tracking
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to keep a written record of actions taken and progress made toward their goals.
states: During and after action plan development.

micro_actions.name: Review and reinforce progress
micro_actions.description: Regularly check in on completed steps, troubleshoot any issues, and validate small wins.

name: Cognitive Restructuring and Socratic Questioning
description: Therapist helps the patient identify 'hot' automatic thoughts, evaluate evidence for and against these thoughts, and generate alternative, balanced alternatives through structured questioning.

goal.objective: Reduce cognitive distortions and foster more adaptive thinking.

success_levels.ideal: Patient independently uses CBT techniques to challenge and balance thoughts.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient participates in restructuring thoughts with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient resists or fails to challenge maladaptive thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes or records alternative/balanced thoughts, reduced negative mood ratings.

states: Patient displays distressing automatic thoughts and emotional reactivity.
Patient completes mood/thought identification and is ready for cognitive testing.
Repeated patterns of negative thinking are present.

micro_actions.name: Identify and label automatic/hot thoughts
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to articulate specific automatic thoughts linked to intense emotions and to mark the 'hot' thought.

micro_actions.name: Guide evidence gathering for and against hot thoughts
micro_actions.description: Ask structured questions to elicit factual, objective evidence supporting and contradicting the identified thought.
states: When patient is stuck in a negative belief.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Socratic questioning and challenge
micro_actions.description: Gently ask probing, clarifying, or perspective-taking questions (e.g., 'What would you tell a friend in this situation?') to stimulate critical thinking.
states: Patient is perseverating on unhelpful or distorted thoughts.

micro_actions.name: Prompt generation of alternative, balanced thoughts
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient to construct and articulate a more balanced thought, and discuss the predicted effects of these new perspectives.
states: Patient is ready to test alternative thinking.

micro_actions.name: Support rating and tracking beliefs and emotions
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to rate the intensity of mood and belief in 'hot' and alternative thoughts before and after restructuring.

micro_actions.name: Troubleshoot and review cognitive restructuring process
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively review the process if mood does not improve, checking for missing steps or errors, and encourage repeated practice.

name: Behavioral Experimentation and Activation
description: Therapist collaboratively designs and supports real-life experiments to test beliefs, assumptions, or coping strategies. Also includes systematic behavioral activation planning to improve mood.

goal.objective: Test and update dysfunctional beliefs, increase adaptive behaviors, and/or boost mood.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes experiments, reflects, and modifies beliefs/behaviors accordingly.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts planned activities and discusses findings regardless of outcome.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids behavioral assignments or interprets outcomes in a distorted fashion.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes agreed activities and modifies interpretations based on results.

states: When key beliefs or avoidance patterns have been identified.
Depressed, anxious, or avoidant patient needs behavioral activation.
Patient is ready for practical, experiential learning.

micro_actions.name: Collaborate on designing behavioral experiments
micro_actions.description: Help the patient articulate the belief or assumption to be tested and co-create a concrete experiment targeting it.
states: Patient is open to testing hypotheses.

micro_actions.name: Elicit specific predictions
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to make clear, testable predictions about what will happen during the behavioral experiment.

micro_actions.name: Break experiments into manageable steps
micro_actions.description: Support the patient in detailing each step of the experiment and problem-solve anticipated barriers.

micro_actions.name: Prompt careful recording and review
micro_actions.description: Encourage the patient to record what was done, describe actual outcomes, and to reflect on discrepancies between prediction and reality.

micro_actions.name: Coach and support in-the-moment behavioral activation
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to engage in planned activities, offer encouragement, and help them notice and record enjoyment or accomplishment.
states: Behavioral activation for depression or avoidance.
Skill practice in session or between sessions.

micro_actions.name: Encourage reflection and update of beliefs/behaviors
micro_actions.description: Facilitate discussion of what was learned from experiments, specifically changes in beliefs, mood, or activation.
states: Ongoing learning from exposure or activity.

name: Core Belief Identification and Modification
description: Therapist supports the patient to uncover global, absolute core beliefs, evaluate their impact, and develop and strengthen more adaptive beliefs through exercises and behavioral experiments.

goal.objective: Reveal, challenge, and update core beliefs for sustained change.

success_levels.ideal: Patient clearly identifies negative core beliefs and successfully develops flexible, positive alternatives.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient accepts existence of core beliefs and begins practicing new ones.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient denies or cannot access core beliefs, or refuses to practice updates.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates new core beliefs, tracks belief strength, engages in related activities.

states: After sufficient progress with automatic thought restructuring.
Patient’s difficulties are traced to recurring global belief patterns.
Long-term maintenance and relapse prevention phases.

micro_actions.name: Prompt downward arrow technique
micro_actions.description: Ask targeted recursive questions (e.g., 'If this is true, what does this say about you/others/the world?') to uncover deeper core beliefs.
states: When assumptions and 'hot' thoughts do not reveal underlying patterns.
Patient ready for core belief exploration.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate core belief worksheet completion
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient step-by-step in filling out structured worksheets to document core beliefs, confidence ratings, and behavioral connections.
states: Patient is ready to track and monitor beliefs.

micro_actions.name: Prompt articulation of new, adaptive core beliefs
micro_actions.description: Encourage the patient to state positive, alternative beliefs and relevant behaviors that reinforce these beliefs.
states: After negative core belief has been identified.

micro_actions.name: Support behavioral experiments for core beliefs
micro_actions.description: Assist the patient in planning and conducting experiments to test new beliefs, and record actual outcomes for comparison.

micro_actions.name: Prompt regular ratings and review of belief strength
micro_actions.description: Instruct the patient to periodically rate their confidence in new beliefs and review how these fit with recent experiences.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate gratitude and positive behavior exercises
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to record evidence supporting new beliefs, maintain gratitude diaries, and reflect on positive acts towards themselves and others.
states: Building new habits around positive beliefs.

name: Relapse Prevention Planning and Skill Consolidation
description: Therapist helps patient identify high-risk situations, early warning signs, and actionable prevention plans. Reviews and consolidates skills for ongoing self-management.

goal.objective: Strengthen patient autonomy and decrease risk of setback or relapse.

success_levels.ideal: Patient proactively uses relapse plans and skills to maintain gains post-therapy.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient can identify risk factors and agrees to use skills with reminders.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains passive or ceases CBT skills after symptom improvement.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reviews and updates relapse plans, practices skills independently, seeks help as needed.

states: Late-stage or termination phase of therapy.
Patient demonstrates improvement but requires support in maintenance.
Patient expresses worry about setbacks or has history of relapse.

micro_actions.name: Help identify high-risk situations
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to list situations in which relapse is most likely and describe warning signs in thoughts, behaviors, and emotions.

micro_actions.name: Guide regular self-rating and monitoring
micro_actions.description: Prompt regular mood and skill usage ratings with worksheets to track early warning signs and skill effectiveness.

micro_actions.name: Assist in developing specific relapse prevention plans
micro_actions.description: Collaborate with the patient to design actionable prevention steps tailored to high-risk contexts and warning signs.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate rehearsal and mental imagery exercises
micro_actions.description: Lead mental imagery of skill use in upcoming challenges to build readiness and confidence.

micro_actions.name: Encourage retention and visibility of CBT materials
micro_actions.description: Remind the patient to keep therapy materials accessible for ongoing reference and reinforcement.

micro_actions.name: Review and reinforce gratitude and positive routines
micro_actions.description: Recommend ongoing gratitude journaling and positive behavioral routines to foster resilience.

name: Acceptance and Self-Forgiveness Facilitation
description: Therapist assists patient in developing acceptance of unchangeable thoughts, feelings, or situations and supports self-forgiveness via guided reflection and specific exercises.

goal.objective: Alleviate distress related to guilt, shame, or unchangeable issues by fostering acceptance and compassion.

success_levels.ideal: Patient is able to experience non-judgmental acceptance and self-forgiveness, reducing distress.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts acceptance or self-forgiveness with partial relief.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains stuck in guilt, shame, or distress without progress toward acceptance.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes acceptance, completes reflection exercises, demonstrates reduced self-blame.

states: When evidence supports distressing thoughts/situations that cannot be changed.
Patient struggles with persistent guilt or shame.
Patient is stuck despite cognitive and behavioral attempts.

micro_actions.name: Elicit specific sources of guilt/shame
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to articulate what needs to be forgiven or accepted, including the perceived impact on self and others.
states: Patient expresses ongoing distress over past actions or unchangeable events.

micro_actions.name: Guide detailed reflection and narrative exercises
micro_actions.description: Encourage patient to describe the emotional and practical impacts, ongoing effects, and possible positive changes that can result from acceptance or forgiveness.
states: Patient resists letting go of self-blame.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate compassionate perspective-taking
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to consider how they would view a friend in the same situation, fostering empathy for self.

micro_actions.name: Identify overlooked strengths and positive qualities
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to list personal strengths or positive aspects to support moving forward.
states: Patient feels stuck or hopeless about change.

micro_actions.name: Clarify meaning and process of forgiveness
micro_actions.description: Help the patient distinguish what forgiveness involves and does not involve, supporting realistic expectations.
states: Patient uncertain about forgiveness or confusing it with forgetting/excusing.

micro_actions.name: Prompt creation and review of preventative action steps and monitoring routines
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient to specify high-risk scenarios, develop warning sign awareness, and implement routine monitoring (mood ratings, progress tracking).
